title: Starjob
problem: First-generation immigrants and graduates need guidance to find mentors and apply for their first jobs.
overview: Starjob combines job listings, mentorship, and resources for navigating a new work culture.
role: I was the sole designer, conducting interviews and usability tests and developing the identity, wireframes, and prototypes in Figma.

sections.title: The project

list: Make mentorship and entry-level jobs easy to find.

blocks: Users said they felt more confident applying for jobs.
Designing for multiple screen sizes helped keep career resources accessible across devices.

sections.title: Understanding the user
blocks: Interview participants felt anxious about finding work in a new country. They welcomed mentorship to help them understand the culture and hiring process.
Two personas shaped the work: Chloé, a recent immigrant seeking a job, and Jamal, a student unsure how to apply with little experience.

sections.title: Competitive Audit
blocks: I reviewed competing platforms to identify gaps in career support.

sections.title: Design Process
blocks: I explored screen layouts on paper, then developed wireframes. The home screen gives priority to mentors and job listings, with career resources close by.

sections.title: Usability Testing
blocks: Users valued the interface and career support. Feedback also called for simpler navigation and better accessibility.

list: Support screen readers and keyboard navigation.
Provide descriptive alternative text for images.
Evaluate whether users can find relevant mentors and jobs.
Add resources for job searches and interview preparation.
